customize.text: Scions of the Canopy

The
are a tribe living alongside the Yumkasaurs on Coatepec Mountain. Many millennia ago, they inhabited a site now known as the Ancestral Temple, but after a period of upheaval, they were forced to abandon it. Since the tribe's settlements are now located on a sheer cliff, members of the Scions of the Canopy are renowned for their extreme sports: Free Solo Climbing, Mountain Parkour, Hot Air Balloon Racing, Cliff Bungee Jumping, and much more. Because all tribe members are specially trained, tourists are prohibited from participating in these sports at any time of day without training, instruction, special equipment, and supervision. Their love of extreme sports allows the Scions of the Canopy to be excellent couriers. Using grappling hooks, they can quickly move through trees, delivering packages and letters. During the Abyss's attack on Natlan, Huitztlan couriers relayed reports from the front so warriors could assess the threat. The tribal chief is a relatively young but experienced man named Wayna, whose mantra is, <color=#ffffffd9>"Life isn't complete without taking risks."</color>

The most famous member of the tribe is the Pyro Archon, Mavuika, born over five hundred years ago into an ordinary family. As a child, she was very curious and developed ahead of her peers. One day, when Mavuika was very young, her father went to the Night Warden Wars, where he was to fight the Abyss. His team was victorious, but three of the seven warriors, including her father, perished. Mavuika believed that thanks to the Ode of Resurrection, her father would return unharmed, but contrary to her expectations, he was covered in wounds from head to toe, so much so that he could not even stand on his own two feet. The Ode of Resurrection could rekindle life, but only the fatal wound could be reversed. The wounds that had slowly accumulated as the battle raged on, or pre-existing ailments, would not be cured. Her father told her that this was the truth of "war," that all fear death, but that some would always step forth to fight, because they had something they wished to protect. At that moment, the girl firmly decided that since they were forced to fight that war, she would put an end to it. Her parents supported their daughter, and this acknowledgment only strengthened her resolve and brought the
upon her. And although she later learned many secrets and became more closely acquainted with the crisis that Natlan faced, she never once doubted the trust they placed in her. She believed that this was something that only she could do — not only because she was "Kiongozi" Mavuika, but also because she was her parents' daughter, their pride and joy. She was a daughter of the Scions of the Canopy — a daughter of Natlan.

As a true member of the Scions of the Canopy, Mavuika has a wide range of hobbies and has unparalleled skill in the various sports and games popular across the tribes, constantly striving to improve. When she first learned how to rock climb, she would commit every movement her coach made to memory and ask in detail about every last maneuver. She then trained extensively to make her body remember the trick behind each movement, gradually executing them faster and faster. She also talked with her coach and used various tools and equipment in order to solve problems she encountered, enumerating lists of solutions, and trying out each one in turn before choosing the best. In this way, Mavuika quickly honed her climbing skills, while her questions grew ever harder for her coach to answer, eventually shifting their relationship from that of teacher and student to that of fellow lovers of climbing, delving into their craft together.

customize.text: Yupanqui

The most important and desired Ancient Name of the Scions of the Canopy is
the first bearer of which was Yupanqui, a friend of the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque. Yupanqui was born over two thousand years ago and was born strong, brave, and boastful. In his youth, he wandered the woods, challenging passersby to duels, until one day he was easily defeated by the half-human, Och-Kan, Xbalanque's companion. Seeing the young man in such a pitiful state, the archer laughed. Half of shame, half of annoyance, Yupanqui made up his mind to follow them to hide the shame of defeat.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Hey! You aren't seriously thinking of taking on that... Uh, whatever it is, without me, are you?"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Listen up, you lot! I am Yupanqui, and it is I that is destined to shake the very foundations of the... Wait, I haven't finished!"</color>

More than once did Yupanqui's failure to heed advice land him in great danger, and more than once did his boisterousness earn him his companion's annoyance. Despite this, the companions who journeyed by the warrior's side tolerated his youthful ignorance. Along with five other heroes, they stood against the ancient dragons and journeyed to the Sacred Volcano of Tollan to slay the Pyro Dragon, Xiuhcoatl. After their victory, Xbalanque was reborn from the Sacred Flame and became the first Pyro Archon, and together with his companions, he founded the Grand Alliance.

When Xbalanque, at the dawn of his life, entered the Sacred Flame, he left the rule of Natlan to his best friend, Och-Kan. Attempts to lead humanity to greatness drove Och-Kan to madness, and the capital of the Grand Alliance to the corruption of the Abyss. The half-human, half-dragon hated his dragon side and ordered the extermination of all descendants of the ancient dragons. Lamenting that his grand vision of humans and dragons coexisting had become beyond reach, the aging Yupanqui could not bring himself to rebel against his only surviving old friend. He believed that passion was like fire — despite regret and unwillingness, once extinguished, it is gone. Thus, he silently accepted the idle position of ordnance officer for the Grand Alliance, resolving never to interfere with his old friend's orders again, waiting only for the day that he would return to the Sacred Flame.
But one day, a scarlet-eyed youth from the Flower-Feather Clan decided to rebel against the tyrant Och-Kan. He saved the dragons from the shadow of the sword and, at night, came to pay a visit to the ordnance officer's abode, addressing Yupanqui and begging him to break his oath. The silent old man gave no direct answer, merely glancing at the dusty greatsword beside him. In his eyes, over the long years glazed dull with gloom, a spark of fiery brilliance flashed up once more.

Yupanqui and the scarlet-eyed youth teamed up with the daughter of the mines, Sakkuk, who bore the Ancient Name of Yupanqui's old friend, and the heroic twins, Atawallpa and Waskar. To get into the Forbidden City, they needed a man who knew all the roads, paths, and secret passages of the city and could operate any mechanisms. The silent Yupanqui then named the craftsman Manqu of the Children of Echoes. Manqu managed to cut off power to the Grand Alliance capital, allowing Yupanqui, taking advantage of the confusion, to deliver the scarlet-eyed youth to Och-Kan's throne room. Although the scarlet-eyed youth defeated the tyrant and became the second Pyro Archon, Yupanqui never returned from that rebellion and perished in the Turnfire. According to the legend, Och-Kan used the Turnfire to rule Natlan and oppress anyone who opposed him. Turnfire is different from normal fire: if one gets set on fire with it, they will feel a horrible burning pain from behind them, but they won't die right away. And, whatever you do, you mustn't turn back to look at it. Yupanqui stole the Turnfire and threw it at the Och-Kan's army. All the soldiers were burned to ashes. Just as Yupanqui was about to leave the city, he thought he heard Och-kan calling out to him from behind. It caught him off guard, and he turned around to look, but Och-kan was not there. All he saw was a city burned black, an army in ruins, and giant flames reaching up into the sky. A split second later, the flames he saw burst out from inside his eyes and swallowed Yupanqui up. This fire burned more fiercely than any other. It burned for a hundred days, until it burned a hole right through the Ley Lines, and then fell into the deathly dark Night Kingdom, where it still burns to this day. The Turnfire lights up the path that leads to the next life, but for the dead to be reborn, they have to accept the flames and be purified by the fire first.

customize.text: The War with the Abyss

Five hundred years ago, the Abyss penetrated Teyvat, and all of Natlan was plunged into war. A young warrior of the Scions of the Canopy, Burkina, bearing the Ancient Name Malipo, and his Yumkasaurus companion, Kongamato, joined Burkina's old friend, the exiled Tenoch, and set out to battle the Abyss. Along with Tenoch and other Natlan heroes, bearing the Ancient Names of the first Pyro Archon's companions, they fought in the battle that created the Mare Jivari. During the Cataclysm, Burkina's companion became tainted with the Abyss and lost his mind. In a fit of madness, he attacked Burkina, but the latter did not resist, choosing instead to call upon the power of the Turnfire at the cost of his own life and transfer it to Kongamato. Perhaps he believed the Mountain King was stronger than him and more valuable to the tribe, or perhaps he acted out of loyalty to his friend.

The Pyro Archon, Mavuika, also fought bravely for her country. During the war with the Abyss, the Natlanese calculations estimated that they would have a maximum of five hundred years before the Night Kingdom was completely lost to the Abyss. But at that time, Natlan lay in ruins, and civilization was dying. The tribes needed to be united, otherwise, it would be impossible to dream of a final victory. The Pyro Archon had a long conversation with the heroes of each tribe, and finally developed a five-hundred-year-long plan to save Natlan. During this time, the Archons and chiefs were to rebuild the tribes, and when the time came, the Wayob would again choose six heroes of Natlan with the Ancient Names of Xbalanque's companions. Mavuika herself was to enter the Sacred Flame and be reborn five hundred years later, when Natlan's time was running out.

Five hundred years ago, when Mavuika's plan to save Natlan was revealed to the chiefs and elite warriors, there were stark divisions of opinion. Some believed that the loss of a leader and warrior as important as Mavuika was unacceptable, for there could be no future to speak of if the present era could not be defended. In the end, however, the vast majority were persuaded by Mavuika or by the various tribal chiefs, for hers was the only plan that provided any hope of victory, even though to those at the time, it seemed incredibly risky and had slim odds of success. The warriors visited Mavuika as one, offering their most important belongings to be used as "fuel" in case of any future emergencies. These brave people were proud of this necessary sacrifice and did not hesitate in the least. Mavuika spoke to them each in turn, offering them a hot drink and listening to the stories behind these objects. She wanted to carry these stories with her into the future, for memories can surpass time, where human lifespans may fail. And though these objects might not endure into the future, so long as someone still sang their stories, they could welcome the victorious dawn alongside the people of the future. Some asked the Archon if she had similar stories, and she spoke of her parents, her sister Hine, and two mischievous Yumkasaurs, the things she held most dear in the time she was about to lose. But none of that mattered. All of it ceased to be important the moment they decided on the plan to fight the Abyss, even herself.

Five hundred years later, when Mavuika was reborn from the Sacred Flame, the Abyss once again began its invasion of Natlan. Using the power of the six heroes of Natlan, recognized by their Ancient Names, the power of the divine throne, and the Ruler of Death, Mavuika was able to defeat the Abyss once and for all, but many perished in the war. Among them was the master of intelligence and analysis, Vichama, who bore an Ancient Name, which meant "to seek." During the Night Warden Wars five years ago, Vichama injured his leg and couldn't participate, and his team was unable to overcome the Abyss and perished. Among the dead was Vichama's close friend, Mallko, with whom he had been inseparable. Afterward, Vichama fell into depression and blamed himself for everything. But the battle at the Scions of the Canopy settlement allowed him to fulfill his dream. He scouted the location and direction of the attacks, so Chief Wayna would have the safest way to evacuate. Vichama remained with the tribe until the very end, providing information for the future of his tribe and all of Natlan. He did not fear death, for he knew that in the Night Kingdom he would meet his friend again, and together they would witness the birth of a new Natlan.

customize.text: Malipo

Since the silent warrior Yupanqui died stealing the Turnfire from the tyrant Och-Kan, the Ancient Name
has become the most honorable in Huitztlan. While Ancient Names possess no real power, an Ancient Name scholar from the Scions of the Canopy believed Malipo may represent a special case. Since it first arose during the era of the first Pyro Archon, it may contain remnants of Xbalanque's power. After studying all occurrences of this name, the scholar concluded that Malipo represents a mysterious ritual involving a tit-for-tat exchange with a price. It dated back to the first Pyro Archon, fell with the Grand Alliance, was then buried in the Night Kingdom, and now awaited the call of its new bearer. But this Ancient Name is not only a heroic symbol in Huitztlan, but it also comes with the more ominous implication of eventual tragedy. Every bearer of the name Malipo died of unnatural causes, as if the specter of the Turnfire was always lurking in the background. The researcher believed this indicated the existence of some higher power that is always watching the name-bearer, examining their actions, and eventually demanding payment in return. None can escape this payment — unless, perhaps, they could honestly swear by Turnfire to never make a single mistake in their entire life.

The last bearer of the ancient name Malipo is the Saurian Hunter and hero of Natlan, Kinich. Kinich can be seen everywhere with his companion, the sovereign ruler K'uhul Ajaw, one of the thirteen Dragonlords created by the Pyro Dragon, Xiuhcoatl. His true form was sealed within a bracelet, leaving only a phlogiston projection. One day, an earthquake uncovered ancient dragon ruins rumored to hold a "secret draconic treasure." After more than a few initial surveying parties were lost, however, any interested parties decided to exercise caution. By then, Kinich was already a renowned Saurian Hunter, and one of the teams invited him to join them. It was only after they had entered that they found the place teeming with monsters and mechanisms, discovering that it was far more perilous than the rumors had suggested. Some died, others were wounded, and others still fell back, until at last only Kinich reached the ruin's depths. And that was where he encountered the ancient being, K'uhul Ajaw, who had been sealed away. Kinich immediately sensed the wickedness in the other party's voice, but also realized that its power might be useful even so. As for Ajaw, he desired to see the sun, having spent millennia in the cave. After several days of negotiations, Kinich and Ajaw entered into an unbreakable pact: the dragon pledged to obey Kinich's commands and lend him a share of his strength in accordance with their agreement. In exchange, Kinich took Ajaw with him so he could see the outside world, and upon his death, his body would be given to the sovereign ruler. When Kinich signed the pact, he truly understood what it meant to pay the "price" and received the Ancient Name Malipo.

customize.text: Yumkasaurs

For centuries, the Yumkasaurs have been the faithful companions of the Scions of the Canopy. Together, they battle the Abyss, engage in sports, and deliver packages. The most famous Yumkasaurus and the tribe's symbol is Mountain King Kongamato, a companion of the hero Burkina. They met when Burkina was a young courier. One day, the hero made a bet with the Yumkasaurus that he would climb the farthest peak of Coatepec Mountain and harvest the Flamegranates from the mother tree, which grew higher than the volcano. To carry out his plan, Burkina began training rigorously until he was finally ready for the challenge. He was about to throw a hook to retrieve the Flamegranates hanging from the tree, but a sudden gust of wind threw him back. Burkina began to fall from the tree when, suddenly, a Yumkasaurus appeared in the dense canopy of the Mother Tree and saved the courier from death with its long tongue. The same Yumkasaurus who always tussled with Burkina secretly followed him and saved him at a crucial moment. The young courier gave him the Flamegranates as a token of gratitude, and thus began a friendship between the future hero of Natlan and the Mountain King Kongamato.

After Kongamato was corrupted by the Abyss and killed his friend during the Cataclysm, he fell into slumber. The memories of his friend were lost to a long nightmare, and even the name "Kongamato" itself has become unfamiliar to the ancient lord of the Yumkasaurs. The Abyss energy within him was extremely sensitive, and if disturbed, he would awaken and fly into a blind rage, attacking anything that moved. The Mountain King was unable to break free from the nightmare, but he had to protect the Turnfire, no longer even knowing to whom it belonged. Even if the great body he was once so proud of continues to be wracked by burning agony, even if his now decaying frame still bears the imprints of unbearable shame, even so, he would never allow anyone to desecrate the life and fire that were once his. For the giant beast, now lost to madness, despite his soul having been consumed by the filth of darkness, this final shred of resolve he refused to abandon, no matter what.

<color=#ffffffd9>"I shall return the Turnfire name to the Night Realm, in exchange for the final kindling."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"By past fuel, and present flame, life marches ever on."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"We will answer to the fire for all our deeds. Amidst the flames, we shall be reunited."</color>

The tribe started celebrating a ceremony, the Turnfire Night, during which they remembered the fallen heroes of Natlan and cleansed the Abyss within the Mountain King so that he would remain soundly asleep. Over time, Abyssal activity in Natlan increased, affecting the unstable energy within the Yumkasaurus, causing him to awaken and attack with increasing frequency. Some elders decided to completely purge Kongamato of the Abyss, which would have resulted in the death of the tribe's symbol, but the current bearer of the Malipo name, Kinich, was able to restore the Yumkasaurus's sanity. The Turnfire, summoned by the Mountain King himself, and the Sacred Flame, created a transparent shell around Kongamato, isolating him from the external influence of the Abyss.

This "Mountain King," who once joined forces with the great heroes against the Black Tide, holds a special place in the hearts of the Scions of the Canopy. Some tribe members believe that it has its current body shape because it has a unique physique, like the Qucusaurus "Tyrant"... Though in fact, this is simply because it's lived for so long, and eaten way, WAY too much.

customize.name: Yumkasaur Whelp
customize.desc:
A young Yumkasaurus with the ability to spit Flamegranate pectin hidden in their cheek pouches out, wrapping around distant objects.
Their hold on pectin-coated objects isn't strong enough, nor is their sense of balance good enough to allow them to move freely through the air. Sometimes, they'll even fall over to one side just sitting on their tails. However, one day, they will grow into the form that can swing freely between the trees without a care.

customize.name: Yumkasaurus
customize.desc:
A Saurian with powerful hind legs and a fluffy tail, capable of spitting Flamegranate pectin hidden in their cheek pouches out, wrapping around distant objects.
According to legend, the original Yumkasaurs were not at all like today, but much smaller, so small that they were difficult even to see. They could roam freely with the wind, cling to the bodies of the massive dragons, or gather in groups to move about like clouds. However, in order to maintain their form after their abilities degenerated, they had no choice but to assume their current shape.

customize.name: Kinich
customize.desc: A Huitztlan Saurian Hunter skilled at counting costs.

customize.name: Fang of the Mountain King
customize.desc: A giant sword forged from pure turquoise. Due to its greater weight than most ordinary weapons, it was named for Kongomato the Mountain King.

value.name: "Scions of the Canopy"
value.desc:
"Scions of the Canopy"

"Legend has it that the warriors of the Scions of the Canopy, along with one hundred Yumkasaurs, spent a hundred days and a hundred ropes moving the 'Obsidian Totem Pole,' the symbol of their faith, to its current location."

contents.text: ~2,000 years ago
The future Scions of the Canopy moved from the Ancestral Temple to Coatepec Mountain because of the white earth.
The future hero of Natlan, Yupanqui, later given the Ancient Name Malipo, joined Xbalanque, Och-Kan, and other heroes in battle against the dragons.
Xbalanque became the first Pyro Archon and led the Grand Alliance.
Och-Kan became the ruler of the Grand Alliance and ordered the extermination of all Saurians. The aging Yupanqui accepted a position as an officer in the Grand Alliance.
A scarlet-eyed youth convinced Yupanqui to join him in overthrowing the tyrant Och-Kan.
Och-Kan was overthrown, but Yupanqui died due to the Turnfire, also known as Malipo.
~500 years ago
Burkina, one of the six heroes of Natlan who would bear the Ancient Name Malipo, was born in the Scions of the Canopy.
Mavuika, the future Pyro Archon of Natlan who would bear the Ancient Name Kiongozi, was born in the Scions of the Canopy.
The Yumkasaurus Kongamato saved Burkina and became his companion.
Mavuika won the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame and became the Pyro Archon.
The Cataclysm began.
Burkina and Kongamato joined Tenoch and set out to battle the Abyss.
Kongamato was infected by the Abyss and killed Burkina.
Mavuika entered the Sacred Flame to be reborn after 500 years to save Natlan.
Kongamato went into hibernation, and the tribe began the Turnfire Night ceremony.
Present Day
Mavuika was reborn from the Sacred Flame.
The Abyss attacks became more frequent.
Wayna became the tribe's chief.
The Saurian Hunter Kinich received the Ancient Name Malipo and became one of the six heroes of Natlan.
Five years ago, Mallko from the Scions of the Canopy died along with his entire team during the Night Warden Wars, and his friend Vichama fell into depression.
Kongamato began waking up more frequently and attacking everyone.
Elder Trinidad attempted to completely purge the Abyssal energy from Kongamato during the Turnfire Night to kill him, but was stopped by Kinich.
Vichama helped to find the Ancient Name of the warrior from the Children of Echoes to bring her back from the Night Kingdom.
The Abyss launched a full-scale invasion of Natlan.
Vichama died during the battle and reunited with Mallko in the Night Kingdom.
The Pyro Archon used the power of the six heroes of Natlan, the Ruler of Death, and the divine throne to banish the Abyss.
The Abyss was destroyed.
